A1.justification: Both PDFs present MSU-Bench with readable text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. The retained material can be matched despite substantial appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original zero-shot and LoRA evaluations on MSU-Bench, title-only and batched-question analyses, and MMLU retention results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports judge agreement, bootstrap intervals and model failure cases.

M1.justification: ABC/PDF inputs, three-model majority judging, LoRA adaptation and modality-specific encoder-freezing procedures are retained. Expanded curation and training descriptions do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: The same 150-score list, 1,800 questions, four comprehension levels, ABC/PDF modalities and MMLU evaluation remain. Clarifying that score instances can include movements or excerpts and recategorizing genres do not establish changed data or task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 2 and 5 and the adaptation comparisons is unchanged. v3 corrects the supplementary baseline discussion from Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct to the 7B model already listed in both versions' Table 5.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 revises the stated LSR normalization from cumulative question count to score count. Existing accuracy protocols, training budgets and decoding settings remain unchanged. Added fixed-test-set and exclusion explanations document the retained setup; the PDFs do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: New Appendix L examines three Claude Opus 4 failures on BWV 948 involving pitch identification, cadence judgment and motif localization. Judge-unanimity analysis supplements existing evaluation validation. The title-only, batching and modality ablations are retained.

E5.justification: v3 adds percentile-bootstrap 95% confidence intervals for eight model/modality accuracies in Table 3 and for judge agreement. v2 already reported Wilson LSR intervals and Pearson/McNemar statistics. Single-run reporting remains; additional runs or seeds are not established.

E6.justification: New results include 83.33% judge agreement and three failure outputs. Figure 8b replaces broad genre groupings, such as large-scale works (31%), with categories including character pieces (23%) and sonatas (20%). Existing zero-shot, fine-tuning, title-only, MMLU, timing and LSR results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The LSR definition becomes an average over scores of indicators that every question through level l is correct, replacing v2's question-count denominator. v3 also explicitly sets the Wilson interval sample size to the number of scores. This corrects the formal definition; no new proofs or theorems appear.

C1.justification: v3 withdraws the 'first' and 'first large-scale' benchmark claims from the abstract, introduction and conclusion. The conclusion also narrows ABC's benefit to mitigating part of the difficulty. The benchmark contributions and main empirical claims remain.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly interprets ABC as a structured upper-bound modality, distinguishing it from end-to-end visual understanding. It qualifies the title-only inference as dependence on musical information, replaces 'scaling law' with 'scaling trend', and adds explanations of the new grounding failures.

D1.justification: v3 adds an explicit benchmark/code repository link, documents default MuseScore PDF exports and visible bar numbering, and explains handling of simpler scores. It clarifies that long-score exclusions affect the training pool while the fixed 30-score test set remains unaffected. These are additional disclosures.

R1.justification: v3 adds Chen et al.'s MLLM-as-a-Judge citation and replaces the Ma et al. music-survey citation with Walshaw's ABC standard. It also relinquishes priority claims. Consolidating the duplicate MMMU references does not remove a distinct cited work.

P1.justification: The appendices are substantially reorganized: annotation/recruitment and inference/prompts move earlier, while MMLU moves near the end. Discussions of prompting, baselines, LSR and MMLU are expanded or rewritten, accompanied by widespread copyediting, terminology corrections and author/affiliation updates.

P2.justification: v3 adds the confidence-interval table and two score-excerpt figures, combines the earlier textual and visual LSR displays into Figure 6, and redraws Figure 8b. Most existing displays are retained. Figure 8's caption still describes the old genre categories.

improvement.justification: Correcting the LSR definition, clarifying test-set handling and resource access, and adding uncertainty estimates and failure cases improve interpretability and reproducibility. The narrower novelty and ABC claims are better calibrated. These benefits outweigh limited shortcomings: bootstrap details remain incomplete, and Figure 8's unchanged caption conflicts with its revised genre chart.
